title: Fully differential telescopic OTA
description: A fully differential telescopic-cascode OTA. Each side stacks a tail source, an input device, an NMOS cascode, a PMOS cascode, and a PMOS load between the rails; the cascodes boost the output resistance so a single stage reaches high gain. $A_v = g_{m,in} * R_{out}$, where each side's output resistance is a cascode-boosted branch resistance combined in parallel: looking down, the NMOS cascode multiplies the input device's $r_o$ by its intrinsic gain ($A_{v0,cascn}/g_{ds,in}$); looking up, the PMOS cascode multiplies the load's $r_o$ ($A_{v0,cascp}/g_{ds,load}$). Those branch expressions are the standard cascode approximation (they drop second-order $g_{mb}$ and finite-cascode-gain terms). Being fully differential, there is no current-mirror in the signal path and therefore no mirror pole or its attendant pole-zero doublet — a real frequency-response advantage over the single-ended mirror-loaded stage. Common-mode feedback is required to set the output common mode, but the CMFB loop itself is out of this sheet's scope (no loop solving): it appears only as a current line item $I_{cmfb}$ added to the supply budget. The differential output swing is twice the single-ended cascoded headroom. Internal node levels are authored choice params with per-device saturation invariants. On the demo NMOS table every device sizes against the same data.

params.name: v_margin
params.note: headroom beyond the four stacked cascode vdsat drops (tail saturation plus safety) folded into the swing estimate

params.name: I_cmfb
params.note: current the common-mode feedback network draws; the CMFB loop itself is out of scope (no loop solving here) — this is a supply-budget line item only

params.name: I_tail
params.note: total tail current (each side carries half)

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion (sets gm_in and input noise)

params.name: p_sign
params.note: vds sign of the PMOS device tables: +1 N-style, -1 signed-PMOS

doc.title: Input pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current; its gm sets the stage transconductance and its output conductance is the bottom of the down-looking cascode branch.

doc.title: NMOS cascode device
doc.description: The NMOS cascode over the input device; its intrinsic gain multiplies the input device's output resistance (the down-looking branch of Rout).

doc.title: PMOS cascode device
doc.description: The PMOS cascode under the load; its intrinsic gain multiplies the load's output resistance (the up-looking branch of Rout).

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: PMOS load device
doc.description: The PMOS load carrying the branch current; its output conductance is the top of the up-looking cascode branch.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device carrying the full bias current; its saturation headroom sets the tail-node floor.

rows.name: Rdown
rows.note: down-looking branch resistance: the input device ro boosted by the NMOS cascode intrinsic gain (cascode approximation)

rows.name: Rup
rows.note: up-looking branch resistance: the load ro boosted by the PMOS cascode intrinsic gain (cascode approximation)

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: single-side output resistance = the two cascode branches in parallel. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

rows.name: swing_diff
rows.note: differential output swing = twice the single-ended range left after the four stacked cascode vdsat drops and the tail/safety margin

rows.name: I_q
rows.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the tail plus the CMFB network's budget (the CMFB loop itself is out of scope). The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input-pair thermal noise density, both devices (the cascodes and loads add little when the input gm dominates)

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

rules.note: single-stage cascoded gain meets the target
the differential output swing meets the target
